- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7), especially when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply 2–5% downward bias for first 7 days.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to adjust; apply upward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days to counteract overcorrection.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use 1–2% upward bias for next 3–7 days if price is trending up, or downward if trending down.
